About Kings & Dice

Everything about the game, in one place.

What Kings & Dice is

Kings & Dice is a dice chess game — normal chess, but the dice decide which pieces you must move. Every turn starts by rolling 3 dice. Each die gives you one move of that kind of piece — so up to 3 moves per turn.

You choose the order: tap any die to use it next. Each die can be used once, then it's spent.

If a die's piece has no legal move yet, that die is not lost — it stays for the rest of this turn. Try another die first; that move may unblock it (for example, a pawn moves and a bishop's path opens), and then the first die can be used. A die is only lost when the turn ends — all dice spent, you tap End Turn, or no remaining die can move at all so no move can unblock anything.

Movement is normal chess — castling, en passant and pawn promotion all work as usual — but there is no checkmate. You may move even if it leaves your own King attacked, and you may ignore an attack on your King. An attacked King is marked with a red “!” bubble on its own square — protect it or strike first.

You win by capturing (killing) the enemy King. The game ends the moment a King is captured — even mid-turn, even by a King capturing the other King. Kings may stand next to each other. If a side ever has no movable piece at all, the game is a draw.

Special dice

Special Dice are always on in every game — there is no option to turn them off. Every rolled die has a 15% chance to be a black-and-gold special die instead of a numbered one. Each special is spent like a normal die once used:

  • ★ WILD: move ANY one of your pieces — including killing the King.
  • ⚡ EXTRA: move ANY one of your pieces, then immediately roll one bonus die for this turn.
  • ⚔ CAPTURE: move ANY one of your pieces, but the move must capture an enemy piece. If nothing can capture yet, the die stays for this turn, like a stuck die.
  • 🛡 SHIELD: tap one of your pieces to shield it — it cannot be captured until the start of your next turn. A gold shield mark shows on it.
  • ⇄ SWAP: swap the squares of two of your own pieces. Kings can swap; a pawn may not swap onto the first or last rank, and a King or Rook that swaps loses castling rights.

The dice

1 · Pawn2 · Knight3 · Bishop4 · Rook5 · Queen6 · King

1 = Pawn, 2 = Knight, 3 = Bishop, 4 = Rook, 5 = Queen, 6 = King. The dice tumble on the board when a player rolls — in a Live game, both players see the same roll settle on the same faces.

Match types

Classic
  • Classic: Normal dice chess — the original game. Win by capturing (killing) the enemy King.
Arcade Modes
  • King of the Hill: as well as killing the King, a player wins immediately by legally moving their own King — with a King (6) die — onto any of the four hill squares d4, d5, e4, e5, marked on the board in that variant. The game ends at once, even mid-turn, and it counts as a full win for the coin pot.

Match type, names and stake are all chosen on the setup screen before the game starts — the game screen itself only shows read-only chips for them. Special Dice are always on. In Live rooms and Friend turn codes, the setup travels with the game so both players play by the same choices.

Turn timer: also chosen in setup — 30s, 60s (the default), 90s or Off — and locked at Start. The clock starts when the dice land, pauses while a panel is open, and if it reaches zero the turn passes with unused dice lost. Turn-code games are untimed.

Arcade Modes in detail

Chaos: Special Dice come up half the time (50%). At the start of every 3rd round a random Fate hits both players: Wild Surge (your next roll is guaranteed a WILD die), Shield Rain (both Kings are shielded until their owner's next turn), Extra Dice (your next roll has 4 dice) or Swap Storm (two of each player's own non-King pieces swap places at random). No Fate in round 1.

Double Kings: each side starts with two Kings — the queenside Knight is replaced by a second King. Only the original e-file King may castle. Capturing the first enemy King does not end the game ("One King down! One to go.") — you win by capturing both. The red ! marker appears on either King that is under attack.

Horde: White is the Horde — 24 pawns filling the first three ranks and no King. Black is the standard army. For the Horde, every rolled die counts as a Pawn die; pawns promote on the last rank as usual, and a promoted piece then moves only on its own matching die. Pawns double-step only from the second rank. The Army wins by capturing every Horde piece; the Horde wins by capturing the Army's King. Against the Computer you choose which side to play.

Random Royals: on Start, each side's back rank is arranged in a random order — bishops always land on opposite colours, and the same arrangement is mirrored for both sides, so it is fair. The arrangement is made once by the host/creator and travels in turn codes and Live rooms. Castling is disabled in this mode.

Shrinking Board: after every 5 full rounds the board's outer ring burns away and becomes lava — anything standing on it is removed, and if a King burns, its owner loses (both Kings burning together is a draw). Lava squares are out of play: nothing can move onto them and sliders stop at them. During the round before a burn, the doomed ring glows and the turn banner counts down.

Zombie: Captured pieces wait in the graveyard (the captured-piece rows by the board). When you roll a WILD die, you may spend it to resurrect one of your own captured pieces — never a King — onto any empty square of your own first two ranks, instead of moving. A captured King still ends the game as usual.

Royal Guard: the classic check rules — these apply only in this mode; every other mode still wins by capturing the King. In Royal Guard no move may leave your own King attacked, so the King can never actually be captured and Kings can never stand next to each other. Giving check ends your turn immediately — any remaining dice are lost, even on a discovered check. When your turn starts in check, you roll as normal but only escape moves count (move the King, capture the attacker, block the line, or take a checking pawn en passant — castling out of, through or into check is illegal). Any die that cannot be used in an escape can be rerolled once with the gold button under the board. If no escape exists at all, it is checkmate before you roll; if escapes exist but your roll and reroll give you no die to play one, it is checkmate by dice. Not in check but with no legal move at all is stalemate — a draw; having moves that simply don't match your dice just passes the turn, as in every mode.

Ways to play

  • Online — Live Online: create a room, share the 5-letter code, and play live. Normal and King of the Hill run on the Kings & Dice server — it rolls the dice itself, validates every move, tracks server coin balances, and holds your seat for 60 seconds if your connection drops. Every other match type uses Friend (P2P) rooms over a free public peer relay, where connected players can also chat in the room (chat is P2P-only and kept only for that session). Turn codes are the backup that always works.
  • Online — Play a Friend: swap turn codes by message. After your move, send your code; your friend pastes it in, takes their turn, and sends a code back.
  • Offline — Vs Computer: you play White against the computer on this device.
  • Offline — 2 Players: take turns with a friend on the same device.

Virtual coins

Each player starts with 1,000 fun coins. Pick a stake before a match — 0 for no betting, a preset, a custom amount, or All-in, capped at the lower balance. Both sides stake the same, the pot is both stakes together, the winner takes the pot and a draw returns both stakes. Balances reset to 1,000 for free if someone hits zero.

Virtual coins only — no real money. Nothing is bought, paid or cashed out.

Radio & voice

Radio: the menu 📻 bar plays one station, House — “Nothing” by RetroBlue, streamed on loop from the game's own site (so it needs internet) — plus Off. Your choice is saved on this device, plays on menu and setup screens, and in a match only if you turn it on from the in-game 📻 button. It is purely local and never syncs to your friend.

Voice: in Live Online rooms (server rooms and Friend rooms alike), the 🎤 button starts an audio-only voice chat with your friend — the mic only opens when you tap, nothing is recorded, and headphones are recommended. Voice Controls (Settings, off by default) add a 🎙 button in any match: tap it and say “roll”, “knight”, “e2 to e4”, “end turn”, “undo” or “flip board” — listening only starts on your tap and nothing is stored by the game.

Learn to Play

Short steps, in the order you'll actually do them.

Tutorial completed ✓ A short guided match on a small board — real dice, real moves, a coach beside you. No coins, no stats, skip anytime.
  1. Pick a mode and startChoose Online or Offline on the main menu, pick Normal or King of the Hill, then set your name and stake in the setup panel next to the board.
  2. Roll 3 dice on the boardTap Roll 3 dice. The dice tumble right on the board and settle — those 3 dice are your moves for this turn.
  3. Tap a die — any orderTap any one of your rolled dice first. Its number says which piece you move:1 · Pawn2 · Knight3 · Bishop4 · Rook5 · Queen6 · KingThe die tells you its piece — for example, “You move a Knight.” Each die is used once.
  4. Tap a glowing piece, then where it goesYour pieces of that type that can move glow. Tap one, then tap a highlighted square to move it there.
  5. A stuck die stays — it isn't lostIf a die's piece can't move yet, the die stays for this turn. Example: your Bishop is blocked by your own pawn. Use your Pawn die first to move the pawn — the bishop's path opens, and now that same Bishop die works.
  6. How a turn endsYour turn ends when all 3 dice are spent. In a hurry? Tap End Turn to pass — any dice left are lost then, and only then. Then it's the other player's roll.
  7. Beat the clockSetup offers a turn timer — 30s, 60s (the default), 90s or Off — locked in at Start. The clock starts when your dice land; if it runs out, your turn passes and unused dice are lost. Turn-code games have no timer.
  8. How you win — kill the KingYou win by capturing the enemy King. There is no checkmate: a King under attack gets a red “!” bubble on its square but the game goes on — you can even leave your King attacked. In King of the Hill, you also win the moment your King legally lands on a centre hill square — d4, d5, e4 or e5.
  9. Special diceSpecial Dice are always on — a rolled die can come up special instead of numbered: ★ WILD move any piece · ⚡ EXTRA move any piece, then roll a bonus die · ⚔ CAPTURE move any piece but it must capture · 🛡 SHIELD protect one of your pieces from capture until your next turn · ⇄ SWAP trade the squares of two of your pieces.
  10. Stakes and the potBefore a match, both players stake the same number of virtual coins. The pot is both stakes together — winner takes the pot, a draw gives both stakes back. Virtual coins only, no real money.
  11. Try the other match typesThe setup screen offers 9 match types. Chaos has specials at 50% with a random Fate every 3rd round. Double Kings — capture BOTH enemy Kings. Horde — White is 24 pawns; every die moves a pawn. Random Royals — shuffled back rank, and castling is disabled. Shrinking Board — the edge burns after every 5 rounds; get your King off the ring. Zombie — spend a WILD die to resurrect a captured piece onto your first two ranks. Royal Guard — the classic check rules: your King must be protected, giving check ends your turn, a checked player may reroll useless dice once to find an escape, and checkmate wins. Every mode works vs Computer, 2 Players, by turn code and in Live rooms.
  12. Join a friendLive: one of you taps Create Room and sends the other the room code; they enter it under Join Room and you're playing live. Once connected, tap Chat to message each other in the room. Backup: use Play a Friend — after your move, send the turn code by message; your friend pastes it in, moves, and sends a code back.
  13. Tune the radio — and try voiceThe 📻 radio bar on the menu plays one station, House — “Nothing” by RetroBlue on loop, streamed from the game's site (needs internet) — or Off. In a Live room, tap 🎤 for voice chat with your friend (mic opens only on your tap; headphones recommended). Turn on Voice Controls in Settings and a 🎙 button appears in matches: tap it and say “roll”, “knight”, “e2 to e4” or “end turn” to play hands-free.

Names, match type, turn timer and stake — locked in when you tap Start. Special Dice are always on.

Special Dice · Always On
Special Dice are always part of the game — every rolled die can come up special instead of numbered. There is no off switch.
Computer difficulty · Medium
The computer plans its whole 3-dice turn — move order, repeated pieces, captures and King safety. Easy plays fast and loose; Hard also looks ahead to your best reply.
Turn timer · 60s per turn
One clock per turn, starting when the dice land. If it runs out, the turn passes and unused dice are lost. It pauses while a panel is open.
No timer in turn-code games — turns are played when you can, so the clock doesn't apply here.

After your move, copy the turn code and send it to your friend (WhatsApp, text, anything). They open Kings & Dice, pick Play a Friend, paste your code below, and take their turn — then send a code back to you.

Live online

Server rooms (Normal & King of the Hill) run on the Kings & Dice server: it rolls the dice and validates every move — no client can pick its own dice, move out of turn, or replay a move. If a connection drops, your seat is held for 60 seconds to rejoin. Friend (P2P) rooms below remain for every other match type and as a fallback. Turn codes always work too.
